subject: Variable fitness ranges on different instances

messages.author: ba39eca4349c4b40
messages.subject: Variable fitness ranges on different instances
parts:
Hi,

I have instances that correspond to different datasets for a classifier, so the range of fitness values for each instance is very different. Does irace compare the fitness of a parameter set across all instances? This is a heterogeneous scenario; I am looking for a good configuration over all instances. I can't seem to see from the user manual how instances play into the statistical comparison of parameter sets, except that I should be using elitist irace.

Thanks in advance for the help

messages.author: 1e8700780c0e6d69
messages.subject: Re: Variable fitness ranges on different instances
parts:
Hello Dennis, 

As explained in section 10.r of the user guide:
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/irace/vignettes/irace-package.pdf
the Friedman test is test is the one we advise to use when the scale of the results of the executions are not meaningful, which is your case.  

The default statistical test used by irace is the Friedman test, so the default setting of irace should be adequate.

If you have a heterogenous scenario, that is, the configurations that are good for a subset of the instances are not good for the rest,  we advise to adjust the default settings of irace to ensure that there is enough information of the performance of the algorithm when performing the statistical test. For details about this please see Section 10.4 of the user guide. 

I hope this is useful for you, 

Let us know if you have more questions!
Bests,
Leslie.
